messages:
maria: quick heads-up — after yesterday's auth-refactor deploy I'm seeing project-scoped roles propagated to org scope for several new workspaces. possible RBAC propagation bug :grimacing:
ian: ack, can you paste an example workspace_id + binding?
maria: example -> workspace=ws_9f3a, binding: {role: "project.viewer", scope: "org:org_12"} — should be scope: "project:ws_9f3a"
raj: that matches the normalizer change we merged. PR #4523 changed scope normalization. pinging the dev who merged
sam_devex: deploy-bot: which services rolled yesterday?
security-bot: deploy 2026-03-19T22:40 UTC to auth-service, policy-normalizer v2.1.0 by @dev_contrib
ian: running a quick audit query to get scope of the damage:
```
SELECT org_id, workspace_id, role, count(*) FROM role_bindings
WHERE created_at >= '2026-03-19' AND scope LIKE 'org:%' AND role LIKE 'project.%'
GROUP BY org_id, workspace_id, role;
```
maria: query results (summary): 8 orgs, 23 workspaces, earliest offending binding at 2026-03-19T22:41UTC. most common: org_12 -> ws_9f3a (3 bindings)
raj: severity? if any of those orgs are customers and had cross-org access that's bad. do we have evidence of api calls using the wrong scope?
maria: yes — audit logs show a few reads from a user in org_12 hitting ws_9f3a resources at 22:45UTC (see sample line below)
```
[2026-03-19T22:45:12Z] auth: allow user:u_832 action:read resource:workspace/ws_9f3a reason:role=project.viewer scope=org:org_12
```
ian: mitigation plan: 1) turn off role-propagation feature flag, 2) revoke org-scoped project.* bindings, 3) rollback policy-normalizer to v2.0.9 if needed. I can run revoke script.
ian: revoke dry-run command:
```
python ops/scripts/revoke_bindings.py --filter "role=project.viewer AND scope LIKE 'org:%'" --dry-run --output csv
```
maria: please dry-run first and post CSV to S3 for legal/cs review before actual revoke
ops-oncall: we can also flip auth-service back to image 2.0.9 if revoke risks breaking live traffic. standby to rollback.
sam_devex: revert PR has been opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-service/pull/4590 (revert policy-normalizer change)
security-bot: incident created INC-2026-0320-01 severity=sev2 owner=ian
ian: running dry-run now... found 23 offending bindings, creating CSV to s3://redwood-incidents/inc-2026-0320-01/exposed_bindings.csv
maria: uploaded sample audit lines and CSV. sharing with legal and cs. s3://redwood-incidents/inc-2026-0320-01/artifacts.zip
raj: before revoking, do we have any customers actively using those workspaces? need to coordinate cs contact
maria: CS list compiled — 4 customers affected. notifying CS lead.
ian: executing revoke at 2026-03-19T22:58UTC
```
python ops/scripts/revoke_bindings.py --filter "role LIKE 'project.%' AND scope LIKE 'org:%'" --apply --confirm
```
ops-oncall: revoke executed, 23 bindings removed at 22:58:34 UTC. starting rollback to auth-service v2.0.9 to be safe.
security-bot: deploy rollback started by ops-oncall (rollback-id rb-20260319-01)
ian: monitoring auth logs for any auth regressions. also adding temporary RBAC alert: detect any future project.* -> org:* bindings.
raj: root cause hypothesis: policy-normalizer inverted "default_deny" handling for project scopes causing normalization to drop project prefix and reformat scope as org when workspace id missing in transform. no unit/integration tests caught it.
sam_devex: follow-ups: add unit tests for scope-normalizer, add integration test with simulated orgs, add CI gate to detect project->org scope migration, and add audit rule to surface suspicious scope transforms.
maria: customer comms template in #incidents-notices, legal reviewing draft. hold public disclosure until legal approves.
ops-oncall: monitoring shows no further org-scoped project bindings post-revoke. will keep 24h watch.
ian: postmortem: I'll own. preliminary timeline and RCA to be posted in #postmortems by EOD tomorrow. immediate fixes: revert normalizer PR, add test cover, and backfill audit alerts.
maria: thanks team. note: we've flagged affected API tokens and rotated service keys for the auth-service integrations as precaution.
ops-oncall: marking incident as resolved in PD once 24h monitoring window completes :white_check_mark:
